label: late copy phase (last two outputs), token-modulated
explanation: Fires only in the copy phase (t > L), never during original tokens or on <DEL>, and only on repeated (not first-occurrence) inputs. Active steps concentrate on the last two outputs (to_go<=1 holds ~71% of mass), but only ~21% of such steps fire, so precision is poor. Strongest and most reliable for L=3 at the final step (recall_idx=2, 100% firing, holds the top activations); L=5 rarely fires. Magnitude and firing probability depend on the current input token: x and r give the highest rates (x 4x lift), then f, e, g, o, z, l, digit 0. Adding a token list raised F1 only to ~0.39. The remaining dependence on L, t and token identity was not captured by any simple predicate.
